newsitem.title: UK: B.Borneo gives Morpeth go-ahead, to use TLP.
newsitem.headline: B.Borneo gives Morpeth go-ahead, to use TLP.

text.p: British Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc, a fast-growing company engaged in oilfield development, said on Monday its board had approved its $210 million plan to develop its Morpeth field in the deep water Gulf of Mexico.

"Morpeth will be the first field developed using a SeaStar mini tension leg platform (TLP), which will be supplied by deep water alliance partner The Atlantia Corporation of Houston, Texas," the British-based company said in a statement.
British-Borneo said last month that it was convinced by test well data from Morpeth to go ahead with development plans.

Production from the field is scheduled to commence in the summer of 1998 at an expected annual average plateau production rate of 35,000 barrels per day of oil and 35 MMSCF of gas per day, plus associated natural gas liquids and condensate.
Commenting on the alliance with Atlantia, chief executive Alan Gaynor said the project represented its first fruits, "and we hope to conclude further deals using the SeaStar system".
